items.title: Virginia Mayhew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2022
items.q: Ingrid Jensen and I were playing a lot together then

ctx.x: It’s an interesting concept to try to capture an event or a really incredibly strong emotion in music.

Well I agree with that. It was really just one tune and it was a tune by Kenny Barron called “Phantoms” and I just felt like I think if we play this rubato — Ingrid Jensen and I were playing a lot together then and we just played this rubato and just — I didn’t say anything to them about it but that’s sort of what I was going for was phantoms, like what happened that day. But I didn’t write a whole project about it and I didn’t really set out to do it, it was just — it just came to me. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
Did you have a number of — I can remember specific recordings when I was younger that I didn’t know the term “epiphany” yet, but they gave me one.
